title_en: The Story of Dragon Boat Festival
full_text_zh:
[P1] 端午节的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 端午节的故事

司南/改编
秦龙/绘画

连环画出版社

很久以前，在中国的土地上
有许多小国。其中有个楚国，楚国
有个大臣，名叫屈原。

[P3] 楚国旁边有个秦国。秦国有统一天下的野心，
把楚国当做最大的敌人。

屈原向楚王提出许多治理国家的好主张，
可楚王就是不听，屈原非常伤心。

[P4] 后来，楚王中了秦国的奸计，罢了屈原的官，还把他赶出了京城。
屈原离开京城，来到了汨罗江边。他想到国家的前途，想到老百姓的苦难，心里难过极了。他一边走着，一边悲叹：“长太息以掩涕兮，哀民生之多艰。”

[P5] 汨罗江边的一位老渔夫认出了屈原，请他住在自己的茅棚里。
屈原眼巴巴地等待着来自京城的消息。他多想再回到楚王身边，为国家尽力啊！

[P6] 屈原等啊，盼啊，可楚王总也没召
见他，逃难的百姓却越来越多了。
一天，屈原问一个逃难的老头儿：“京城怎样
了？”老头儿颤巍巍地说：“唉，秦国的兵已经打进了
京城。我们……我们已经亡国了！

[P7] 听到国家遭难的消息，屈原
万念俱灰。

[P8] 五月初五的晚上，屈原抱着一块大石头，一头扎进了汨罗江。
老百姓划着船去寻找屈原。可是，江水滚滚，屈原在哪里？人们划啊，划啊，月亮落下去了，不见屈原的影子；太阳升起来了，还是不见屈原的影子。

[P9] 人们悲伤地喊着屈原的名字，用苇叶包上蒸熟的饭团，扔进江里。
“鱼儿啊，要吃就来吃我们的粮食吧，不要去伤害屈原先生的身体啊。”
人们悲伤地喊着屈原的名字，把雄黄酒倒进江中。
“毒虫啊，喝了这酒，就乖乖地醉倒吧，不要去咬屈原先生的身体啊。”

[P10] 大家找了几天
几夜，也没有找到
屈原。男女老少，
都悲伤地哭了。

为了纪念屈原，人们把他投江
的五月初五这一天定为端午节。

[P11] 每年的这一天，人们都要吃用苇叶
包成的粽子，喝雄黄酒。
在南方许多地方，人们还要赛龙舟。
看！江上的龙舟，一只比一只威风。

[P12] 端午节包粽子、赛龙舟的活动，
都是对屈原的纪念。屈原爱国家，爱
百姓，人们永远不会忘记他。

端午节也叫端阳节、五月节。很多人都知道，这个节日的起源，和伟大的诗人屈原有关。
比如赛龙舟。当时楚国人听说屈原投江后，
许多人划船追至洞庭湖，这就是赛龙舟的起源。
以后，每年的五月五日，都以赛龙舟纪念屈原。
大家盼望，龙舟的桨能驱散江中之鱼，这样鱼就不会吃掉屈原的身体。
再比如吃粽子。楚国人在五月五日这一天，
将煮好的糯米饭投入江中，祭祀屈原，因为担心
饭被鱼吃掉，所以他们用竹筒盛装糯米饭，以
后，又逐渐用粽叶替代竹筒包裹糯米。
和许多节日一样，端午节也有特有的食物。
看看这段优美的黄梅戏唱词：“好发把糯米粽摆在
桌上，小碟内装的是桂花白糖。粉蒸肉炒黄鳝佐
料老酱，咸鸭蛋大蒜头酒拌雄黄。”
这些都是江浙地区端午节的美食，别说吃了，光看看，都好像能闻得到诱人的香味儿……

[P13] 除此之外，端午节与蟾蜍（也就是癞蛤蟆）的关系也很密切呢。在古代，端午节是采药、储存药的节日。在中医看来，蟾蜍治疗皮肤病的效果很好，所以，古代端午节采药的时候，一个很重要的活动就是捕蟾蜍。北京有句老话说：“癞蛤蟆，拖不过五月五。”说的就是这个意思。

说完了癞蛤蟆，再说说艾草。艾草能治很多病，被人称为中医之草。除了治病，以前的很多人家还把艾叶挂在门上，用来辟邪。

端午节不仅是中国人重要的节日，也是中国周边国家的重要节日。端午节是日本的男儿节，端午节前半个月左右，日本有男孩的家庭，就会挂出一面面鲤鱼旗，企盼家中的男儿顺利成长。端午节的很多习俗，也传到了韩国，韩国人也在这一天纪念屈原、吃粽子。而在越南，端午节的清晨，爸爸妈妈会为孩子准备好各种美食——糯米酒酿、黄姜糯米饭、杨桃、李子等酸酸的水果，大人们则要喝雄黄酒。

说了这么多，关于端午节，还可以再说上一箩筐！
full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of the Dragon Boat Festival
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P2] The Story of the Dragon Boat Festival

Adapted by Si Nan
Illustrated by Qin Long

Lian Huan Hua Publishing House

Long ago, on the land of China,
there were many small states. Among them was the state of Chu, and in Chu
there was a minister named Qu Yuan.

[P3] Next to the State of Chu was the State of Qin. Qin had the ambition to unify the world,
and regarded Chu as its greatest enemy.

Qu Yuan proposed many good ideas for governing the country to King Chu,
but the king refused to listen, and Qu Yuan was very heartbroken.

[P4] Later, the King of Chu fell for Qin's treacherous plot, dismissed Qu Yuan from his post, and drove him out of the capital.
Qu Yuan left the capital and arrived at the banks of the Miluo River. Thinking of his country's future and the suffering of the common people, he was heartbroken. As he walked, he sighed sorrowfully: "I sigh deeply and wipe away my tears, grieving the hardships of the people."

[P5] An old fisherman by the Miluo River recognized Qu Yuan and invited him to stay in his thatched hut.
Qu Yuan waited anxiously for news from the capital. How he longed to return to the King of Chu's side and serve his country!

[P6] Qu Yuan waited and waited, hoping the King of Chu would summon him, but the number of fleeing civilians kept growing.
One day, Qu Yuan asked an elderly refugee, "How is the capital?" The old man trembled as he replied, "Alas, the Qin army has already entered the capital. We... we have been conquered!"

[P7] Hearing the news of his country's disaster, Qu Yuan
was utterly despondent.

[P8] On the evening of the fifth day of the fifth month, Qu Yuan, holding a large stone, plunged into the Miluo River.
Common people rowed boats to search for Qu Yuan. But the river flowed on, where was Qu Yuan? They rowed and rowed, the moon set, yet no trace of Qu Yuan; the sun rose, still no trace of Qu Yuan.

[P9] People sorrowfully called out Qu Yuan's name, wrapped steamed rice balls in reed leaves, and threw them into the river.
"Fish, if you want to eat, come eat our food, but don't harm Master Qu Yuan's body!"
People sorrowfully called out Qu Yuan's name, pouring realgar wine into the river.
"Poisonous insects, drink this wine, get drunk and lie down obediently, don't bite Master Qu Yuan's body!"

[P10] Everyone searched for several days
and nights, but couldn't find
Qu Yuan. Men, women, old and young,
all cried sorrowfully.

To commemorate Qu Yuan, people set the day he jumped into the river,
the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, as the Dragon Boat Festival.

[P11] On this day every year, people eat zongzi wrapped in reed leaves and drink realgar wine.
In many places in the south, people also race dragon boats.
Look! The dragon boats on the river, one more magnificent than the next.

[P12] The activities of making zongzi and racing dragon boats during the Dragon Boat Festival are all in memory of Qu Yuan. Qu Yuan loved his country and the people, and people will never forget him.

The Dragon Boat Festival is also called Duan Yang Festival or May Festival. Many people know that the origin of this festival is related to the great poet Qu Yuan.
For example, dragon boat racing. When the people of Chu heard that Qu Yuan had jumped into the river, many rowed boats to Dongting Lake, which is the origin of dragon boat racing.
Afterwards, every May 5th, people race dragon boats to commemorate Qu Yuan.
Everyone hopes that the oars of the dragon boats can scatter the fish in the river, so that the fish will not eat Qu Yuan's body.
Another example is eating zongzi. On May 5th, the people of Chu threw cooked glutinous rice into the river to worship Qu Yuan, because they were afraid the rice would be eaten by fish, so they used bamboo tubes to hold the glutinous rice, and later gradually used bamboo leaves to wrap the glutinous rice.
Like many other festivals, the Dragon Boat Festival also has its own special foods.
Take a look at this beautiful Huangmei Opera lyric: "Good to put glutinous rice zongzi on the table, small dishes contain osmanthus sugar. Steamed pork with yellow eel, seasoned with old sauce, salted duck eggs, garlic, and wine mixed with realgar." 
These are all delicacies of the Dragon Boat Festival in Jiangsu and Zhejiang regions. Forget eating them, just looking at them, you can almost smell the tempting aroma...

[P13] In addition, the Dragon Boat Festival has a close connection with toads (also known as frogs). In ancient times, the festival was a day for collecting and storing herbs. In traditional Chinese medicine, toads are believed to be very effective in treating skin diseases. Therefore, catching toads was an important activity during the herb-gathering period of the Dragon Boat Festival. There's an old saying in Beijing: 'Frogs can't last past the fifth day of the fifth month.' This is exactly what it means.

After talking about frogs, let's discuss mugwort. Mugwort can treat many illnesses and is known as the 'herb of traditional Chinese medicine.' Besides medicine, many families in the past would hang mugwort leaves on their doors to ward off evil spirits.

The Dragon Boat Festival is not only an important holiday for Chinese people but also for countries surrounding China. In Japan, it is known as Boys' Day. About half a month before the festival, families with boys would hang carp streamers, hoping their sons would grow up healthily. Many customs of the Dragon Boat Festival have also spread to Korea, where people commemorate Qu Yuan and eat zongzi on this day. In Vietnam, on the morning of the festival, parents prepare various foods for their children—sweet rice wine, ginger glutinous rice, starfruit, plums, and other sour fruits, while adults drink realgar wine.

After saying all this, there's still so much more to say about the Dragon Boat Festival!
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《端午节的故事》的封面，画面以剪纸风格描绘了多艘龙舟竞渡的场景，下方标有书名和出版社名称。
[P2] 本页为绘本《端午节的故事》的第2页，左侧为书名页，右侧画面描绘了古代楚国场景，并配文介绍很久以前中国有众多小国，其中楚国有位名叫屈原的大臣。
[P3] 本页介绍了楚国与秦国的敌对关系，并描述了屈原向楚王提出治国主张却未被采纳，因而感到伤心的情节。
[P4] 本页讲述了楚王中了秦国奸计，罢免并驱逐了屈原。屈原离开京城后，来到汨罗江边，为国家前途和百姓苦难而悲叹。
[P5] 本页描绘了屈原被流放至汨罗江边后，被一位老渔夫收留，并在茅棚中日夜期盼能重返京城、为国效力的情景。
[P6] 屈原在汨罗江边等待楚王召见，但百姓逃难越来越多；他向一位逃难老人打听京城情况，得知秦国军队已攻入京城，楚国已亡。
[P7] 本页描绘了楚国被攻破、百姓逃难的景象，以及屈原得知国破家亡后万念俱灰的悲痛心情。
[P8] 本页描绘了屈原在五月初五夜晚抱着石头投江自尽，以及百姓们在江上划船寻找他却始终不见其踪影的场景。
[P9] 百姓们为纪念投江自尽的屈原，将用苇叶包裹的饭团投入江中，祈愿鱼儿不要伤害屈原的遗体；同时，有人将雄黄酒倒入江中，祈愿毒虫不要啃咬屈原的身体。
[P10] 本页描绘了百姓在江上寻找屈原未果后悲痛哭泣的场景，并说明人们为了纪念屈原，将他投江的五月初五定为端午节。
[P11] 本页描绘了人们在端午节吃粽子、喝雄黄酒以及在南方赛龙舟的习俗，展现了对屈原的纪念活动。
[P12] 本页介绍了端午节的由来及其习俗，包括赛龙舟和吃粽子，解释了这些活动与屈原的关联，并提及江浙地区的端午节美食。
[P13] 本页介绍了端午节与蟾蜍、艾草的关联，以及该节日在中国周边国家（日本、韩国、越南）的不同习俗，最后总结说关于端午节还有许多内容可讲。
